headline: Overnight range contains a third hour after NVIDIA: Tail eases to 10, Stress elevated into the claims and cash-open block
body: Nasdaq-100 September futures trade at 29,535.25, up 245.75 points or 0.84%, as of 04:16Z against a previous close of 29,289.50. The central observation of this assessment is that the overnight range of 29,432.50 to 29,654.75 is now unchanged for a third consecutive clock-hour and price is sitting close to the middle of it, roughly 120 points below the post-earnings spike high. Three hours have passed without a new session extreme in either direction. That is retracement-rich, contained price discovery: NQ is not holding near an extreme, and no failed retracement has been followed by repeated extension. Regional equities tell the same two-sided story. The Nikkei 225 is 66,358.00, up 0.14%, having opened at 67,097 and traded a wide 65,773.50 to 67,134.50 band before settling back near the middle - a fade and partial recovery rather than an aligned one-way risk-on impulse. The catalyst behind the overnight bid is now fully public and, importantly, two-sided. NVIDIA reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year, non-GAAP earnings of $2.22 per share and a 75.0% gross margin, and guided third-quarter revenue to $108.0 billion plus or minus 2%, with the chief financial officer pointing to roughly 70% fiscal 2028 revenue growth. Against that, the company flagged capacity constraints and extreme memory pricing that are expected to weigh on gross margins later in the fiscal year. The shares rose about 4-5% after hours from a regular-session close of $209.66, itself down 1.59%. A guide-plus-warning combination of that kind typically produces rotation and two-way repricing at the cash open rather than a single persistent leg. Volatility and rates are calm. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00% and near its 14.77 session low, against a 15.84 previous close. The 2-year Treasury yield is 4.17% and the 10-year 4.64% on the 25 August H.15 observation, with Treasury futures marginally bid across the curve, so there is no rates-side stress transmission. WTI is $81.93 and Brent $87.45, both down for a fourth consecutive session on Middle East de-escalation around the Strait of Hormuz; that de-escalation is genuine but reversible. Latest-session internals remain split rather than aligned: megacaps were three up and five down for a mean of -0.22%, while the semiconductor basket was five up and two down. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and support Stress, not index-level mean-reversion failure. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 02:15Z and is therefore outside the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was treated as stale supplementary evidence only; every level cited here was verified independently against primary sources. The macro backdrop keeps Stress elevated at 49: July core PCE held at 3.3% year over year with headline at 3.7%, leaving the policy path unresolved, and Wednesday's Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,224.52, up 0.05%, inside a contained 29,096.84 to 29,296.77 range. Ahead lie U.S. initial jobless claims and the advance goods trade balance at 12:30Z, the 13:30Z cash open, and the Kansas City Fed indices at 15:00Z, with the Jackson Hole symposium opening today and Chair Warsh's first keynote as Chair on Friday at 14:00Z. The forward path therefore holds Tail in the 10-12 band across the remaining Asian and European hours, lifts it to 16 for the claims hour and to 20 for the cash open and the first full cash hour, then decays it back toward 10 overnight.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 hours Claude held Tail in the 10-16 band through the Wednesday European and U.S. sessions, with Stress drifting from 52 up to 61 as the market positioned into July core PCE and the NVIDIA print. Tail stepped to 21 for the 20:00Z hour containing the earnings release, then decayed through 18, 16, 13, 12 and 11 as the initial reaction proved two-sided rather than one-way. Two hourly slots, 21:00Z on 26 August and 00:00Z on 27 August, have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forward window holds Tail in the 10-12 band across the remaining Asian and European hours on the observation that the overnight range has now contained three consecutive hours and mean reversion is available. It rises to 16 for the hour containing initial jobless claims at 12:30Z and to 20 for the cash-open hour and the first full cash hour, which is the only stretch mapped to WATCH, then decays back to 10 through the U.S. afternoon and the overnight session. The published danger window is confined to 12:30Z-15:00Z. Every forecast value beyond the current clock-hour is conditional risk rather than observed structure, and the escalation conditions named in each hour are shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after a failed retracement, and NQ holding near a session extreme.
